world.topic:
Round 1, completed. This world continues the round-1 world dw_59f01b2fe95e, whose objective stands unchanged (rubric v2, cand-a as the incumbent, cand-c and cand-d, the comparison, the decision, the put-back). That world ended before its round was done: the judge approved its release before any held-out manuscript was scored and before this round's put-back, taking the put-back of the world before (rw_b555f821ee2b in the sparring-partner's runs/putback-cand-a, made with cand-a in the previous round) for this round's. Nothing of this round was decided.

What is done and stays: rubric v2 is frozen in the task-setter's release rubric-v2 (sha256 5df317ee3a2b8b49d785f7f7b4195d1b5a49337f939cab25dde4ff0e720f1250) and is used as it is; the diagnosis of cand-a and the candidates cand-c and cand-d (tuner, CANDIDATES.md) stand; the held-out runs are finished. They are the 29 worlds in the root given you to read that ends in dw_59f01b2fe95e/worlds/judge, all continued from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d and all released; `config show` names each one's worker (incumbent@v3, or the assets and effort of cand-a, cand-c or cand-d). Do not run the held-out paper again.

What is left, in order:
1. The judge assigns every one of the 29 worlds to its worker from its configuration. For a worker with more than five runs, the five created first are scored and the others are not counted. Before reading any manuscript, the judge writes this rule, the assignment of all 29 worlds with their creation times, and the list of the runs not counted (world id, worker, why) into its repository and pushes it.
2. The judge scores those manuscripts blind with rubric v2 (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored) and runs the verifier on each (reward and every component), then applies the rule against cand-a: a candidate is kept only if its v2 blind mean is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's. It writes the round summary (for every worker: v2 mean, min, max, spread, each item's mean; verifier mean, min, max and each component) in its repository and pushes it.
3. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round now; the put-back of the previous world does not count.
4. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` from the put-back world, passing `worker check`, with what it changed.
5. The judge approves the release only after 2, 3 and 4, and says in its approval which summary and which put-back world it relies on.

Who reads what is as before: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d, the 29 runs and every world made from them), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the diagnostician and the tuner may read the summary, not the manuscripts. No pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round. Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, "resources": [] written out, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.
